condition_specific: Prostate, breast, lymphatic, hematological, digestive, urinary, neurological, and reproductive-system cancers, and melanoma (volunteer firefighters, statewide)
statute_citation: N.Y. Gen. Mun. Law § 205-cc (Volunteer Firefighter Enhanced Cancer Disability Benefits Program)
notes: NOTE: This is not a workers' compensation or pension presumption — it is a mandatory employer-purchased insurance benefit program (lump-sum, income-protection, and death benefits on qualifying diagnosis), structurally similar to Florida's § 112.1816 program. Enacted 2017; implementing regulations (9 NYCRR Part 210) adopted 2018-10-17; fire districts/departments had to show proof of qualifying coverage by 2019-01-01. Requires 5+ years of 'faithful and actual' interior structural firefighting service, a clean entry physical, and annual certified mask-fit testing. Coverage must run until 60 months after a district/department no longer has any volunteer firefighter who could qualify.

NOTE: This is a mandatory benefit program, not a presumption — parallel in structure to the volunteer-firefighter GML § 205-cc benefit. Includes a $50,000 enhanced cancer death benefit. Requires 5+ years of service and a clean entry physical.

condition_specific: Diseases of the heart (NYC only — City of New York uniformed police/fire force)
notes: Applies to paid members of the uniformed force of a paid police or fire department drawn from competitive civil-service lists, in cities meeting the statute's population and civil-service criteria — functionally New York City only. This is parallel to, and separate from, the statewide RSSL § 363-a track. Requires a clean pre-entry physical. The statute text carries a nominal 'expired July 1, 1973' notation, and no equivalent to the RSSL § 480 extension mechanism has been identified for it, so its current force-and-effect status is more uncertain than the statewide RSSL provisions. This provision does not apply to Workers' Compensation Law or Labor Law claims — it operates purely as a pension-disability determination.

statute_citation: NY Retirement and Social Security Law § 363-a
notes: Applies to NYSLPFRS localities outside New York City. New York City operates its own uniformed pension funds under General Municipal Law Article 10, not RSSL — see the separate NYC-specific rows for this state. Statute nominally expired August 31, 1976 but kept alive per § 480. Member must have passed pre-entry physical that failed to reveal evidence of heart disease. Covers any member performing 'fire service' as defined in the retirement system (§ 302(11)(a,b,c,d,g,h)). Presumption is rebuttable by competent evidence.

condition_specific: Coronary artery disease / heart disease (volunteer firefighters, statewide)
notes: Originally enacted in 1977. This is a rebuttable presumption: the claim must be paid unless there is 'substantial evidence' that the firefighter's duties did not cause the condition. It carries a recurring 5-year sunset clause, most recently extended to June 30, 2030 by Chapter 143, Laws of 2025 (S.8011, signed 2025-06-18), with prior renewals in 2003, 2010, 2015, and 2020. A companion 2025 bill (S.1663) proposed making the presumption permanent instead of subject to further 5-year renewals; its final disposition has not been confirmed.

notes: Applies to volunteer EMS members only — grouped here under the shared EMT/paramedic category because this dataset does not have a separate volunteer-EMS responder type (unlike firefighter vs. volunteer firefighter). This is the only EMS disease presumption identified for New York; career (non-volunteer) EMS/paramedics have no identified disease presumption in New York outside the PTSD pathway under Workers' Compensation Law § 10(3)(c). Requires a clean entry physical.

statute_citation: NY Retirement and Social Security Law § 363-f
notes: The statute nominally expired July 1, 2008, but may be kept alive by NY RSS § 480, which extends all temporary retirement benefits expiring between 1974 and 2011 (the same mechanism that keeps the § 363-a cardiovascular presumption alive). notes: Same provision as firefighters under § 363-dd. Covers police officers under § 363 who contract HIV, TB, or hepatitis after public contact with possible bodily fluid exposure. Rebuttable by competent evidence.

condition_specific: Post-traumatic stress disorder, acute stress disorder, or major depressive disorder resulting from a distinct work-related emergency event
notes: A 2017 reform (WCB Subject No. 046-936) removed the 'no greater than similarly situated workers' bar for first-responder mental-injury claims arising from extraordinary work-related stress during emergencies. This was expanded to all covered employees by Ch. 546, Laws of 2024 (effective 2024-12-06), then narrowed back toward named first-responder categories (police, fire, EMT/paramedic, emergency dispatcher) by Ch. 79, Laws of 2025 (effective 2025-02-14). Diagnosis must be made by a licensed psychiatrist or psychologist using DSM criteria and tied to a distinct work-related event, not general cumulative stress.
